Edward Snowden is a privacy advocate and former intelligence contractor whose 2013 disclosures revealed the scope of global government surveillance programs, sparking an international debate on privacy, security, and civil liberties. Since then, he has become a prominent voice on digital privacy, encryption, and the relationship between technology and individual freedom, contributing to discussions on the societal implications of surveillance in the digital age.

## Pierre Rochard

Pierre Rochard has researched and written about Bitcoin since 2013. He co-founded the Satoshi Nakamoto Institute in 2014 to curate the best primary source literature. In addition to developing open-source Bitcoin software, Pierre is an outspoken advocate for Bitcoin’s decentralized governance. He co-hosts the Noded Bitcoin Podcast and the Bitcoin for Advisors Podcast. Pierre served as the Bitcoin and Lightning product manager at Kraken for three years before joining Riot as the VP of Research.

## Adam Back

Co-founder and CEO of Blockstream, Dr. Adam Back, invented Hashcash, the proof-of-work algorithm cited by Satoshi Nakamoto in the Bitcoin whitepaper, as the future basis for its mining function. Throughout his two-decade-long vocation as an applied cryptographer and security architect, he has held senior roles with a number of technology companies, including Microsoft, EMC, PI, VMware, and Zero-Knowledge Systems, as well as advised many more companies on cryptography and peer-to-peer finance. Dr. Adam Back holds a computer science Ph.D. in distributed systems from the University of Exeter.

It aims to ensure that political decision-makers are always up to date and can adequately consider the impact of Bitcoin on society.

Bitchill is not your typical Bitcoin conference or networking trip. It’s a week or longer Bitcoin retreat in the Caribbean, designed for builders, creators, and free spirits who want to recharge while connecting with like-minded people. Instead of endless panels in hotel ballrooms, you’ll spend your days diving in crystal-clear waters, joining open mic sessions, playing tennis or golf, and sharing barbecues and beers at sunset.

At the same time, Bitchill gives you a soft landing into Próspera, the world’s most Bitcoin-friendly jurisdiction, where you’ll meet residents, explore business opportunities, and see firsthand how life on Roatán blends tropical ease with frontier innovation.

Tickets are priced in Bitcoin (sats) and give you access to the full Bitchill experience.The base ticket (200,000 sats) covers:

• Selected group activities — BBQ nights, pool parties, yoga sessions, open mic talks, and intro experiences

• Full logistical support — we help arrange travel, pickups, and make sure your stay is smooth

• Community integration — meet residents, explore Próspera, and get introduced to the Bitcoin District

Accommodation is not included in the base ticket, so you can choose the housing that best fits your vibe and budget. Prices are for one full week:

• Studio: 90,000 sats/night — private, spacious, ideal for couples

👉 Staying longer? Many participants extend their visit and turn Bitchill into a month-long immersion in Caribbean life and Próspera’s Bitcoin-first community. We can help arrange that too.

• Optional extras such as premium tours or diving certifications

Bitchill is non-profit — every satoshi collected (and often a few more) goes directly into covering accommodation, activities, and event costs.

Próspera is a special economic zone on Roatán, Honduras, built as a hub for innovation, entrepreneurship, and freedom. It’s one of the first places on Earth where Bitcoin is recognized as legal tender, and where you can set up a business, pay taxes, and live fully on a Bitcoin standard.

During Bitchill, you’ll meet residents of the zone, tour the facilities, and learn about opportunities ranging from Caribbean real estate to Bitcoin-friendly company incorporation. Many attendees come away seeing not just a retreat, but a glimpse into what a freer future could look like.

Roatán itself is a tropical paradise: white sand beaches, world-class diving, and a relaxed Caribbean vibe. Unlike mainland Honduras, it’s safe and designed for international visitors, with a growing expat and Bitcoin community.

Bitchill isn’t just a vacation — it’s your entry point into the Bitcoin District in Próspera. This is where Bitcoiners are building a neighborhood and an ecosystem powered by freedom and Bitcoin. You’ll meet locals, see opportunities in residency, business, and real estate, and experience firsthand what it means to live free on Bitcoin in a pioneering jurisdiction.

January is one of the best months to be on Roatán. It sits right after the rainy season and just as the island shifts into its clearest, breeziest, most comfortable period.

• Very little rain — you might get a short shower, but it’s quick and refreshing

• Excellent diving conditions — January typically brings clear water and calmer seas

In short: perfect tropical winter escape. Warm, sunny, and reliable — without the unpredictable downpours of late fall.

If rain happens, it’s usually a brief shower that clears the air and opens up beautiful sunsets. All outdoor activities (beach fires, boat trips, tennis, snorkeling) run normally this time of year.

Meals are self-organized, giving you the freedom to explore the island’s food scene. Roatán has everything from local Honduran street food like baleadas to fresh seafood grills and high-end Caribbean restaurants. Many places in Próspera accept Bitcoin payments via Lightning, while USD cash is widely accepted elsewhere. Group meals are part of the program, too.

Roatán (RTB) has direct international flights from Houston, Miami, Atlanta, Denver, Belize and Guatemala City. Plus great domestic connection in San Pedro Sula.

We’ll be there with pickups, transfers, and local guidance so you never feel lost.

Yes. Most participants are digital nomads or entrepreneurs, so reliable internet is a must. Coliving spaces have solid WiFi, and we also provide SIM backups and Starlink.

There are coworking sessions at the Bitcoin Center in Próspera, but you’re always free to work from your villa terrace, the café, or anywhere else.

Roatán is a Caribbean island that welcomes thousands of international tourists every year. It’s much safer than mainland Honduras, with a strong expat community and infrastructure designed for visitors.

That said, it’s still a developing country: you’ll want to be mindful like anywhere else in Latin America. We’ll guide you on the do’s and don’ts, and you’ll feel comfortable moving around.

Both. Bitchill is about freedom, Bitcoin, and community, but it’s also about sunbeds, cocktails, and beach barbecues. You’ll leave with a tan, new friends, and fresh ideas for building a freer future.

Engineers, developers, product people, marketers and founders can apply, including people without a technical background or prior Zcash experience. The program starts with a tooling walkthrough, and mentors from Zcash projects provide workshops and one-to-one guidance throughout the build day.

Teams can have one to four people. Bring a team or find teammates at the venue. A project can enter both tracks if it meets each track's requirements.

## Tracks and prizes

The organizers advertise USD 5,000 in cash prizes. The published breakdown includes USD 4,800 in competition awards and USD 200 in conditional follow-up bonuses:

- The Zcash Privacy track awards USD 1,300 to the top project, two second prizes of USD 300 each and two third prizes of USD 200 each, totaling USD 2,300 across five projects.
- The Bitrefill Agentic Commerce track requires projects to use Bitrefill. It offers USD 1,000 for the most innovative project, USD 800 for second place, USD 600 for third and USD 100 for the best feedback, totaling USD 2,500.

Both USD 300 Privacy track winners are also named Zcash Ecosystem Prize winners. Each can earn a further USD 100 by agreeing on a milestone relevant to their submission and delivering it publicly. Those two milestone-dependent bonuses account for the remaining USD 200 in the advertised total.

## Schedule

All times are IST (Asia/Kolkata). Luma lists the event from 11:00 on Wednesday 4 November to 15:00 on Thursday 5 November 2026.

Wednesday 4 November is the hack day:

- 11:00: welcome and tooling walkthrough.
- 11:30: building begins, with workshops and mentors.
- Midnight at the end of hack day, listed as 00:00: submissions close.

Judges score every project overnight and select the teams that will demo on stage.

Thursday 5 November is demo day:

- 11:00: top teams announced.
- 12:00: demos and winners announced on stage.

## Food and facilities

Breakfast, lunch and dinner on hack day, plus an afterparty, are included. The venue provides hacking areas, fast internet and group seating. The organizers also advertise merchandise and describe the location as a short tuk-tuk ride from the main Devcon venue.

## After the hackathon

Winning teams will be paired with an ecosystem partner to agree, deliver and publicly share one small milestone within 30 days, with mentorship and support. The organizers say the same milestone-based follow-up is open to builders who do not win.

## Registration and venue

The Hacker Pass is free, but registration requires host approval. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis for the 75 selected places. Participants must be in Mumbai in person on Wednesday 4 November; remote participation is not available.

The public venue is True Tramm Trunk BKC, G2-B, Ground Floor, Trade Centre Bkc, opposite MTNL, G Block, MMRDA Area, Bandra Kurla Complex, Bandra East, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400098, India.

description:

## What to expect

The extension serves as an open collaboration space and cultural bridge:
- Daily co-working sprints with high-speed internet, collaborative whiteboards, and private meeting zones.
- Pop-up technical salons discussing crypto-native culture, network states, public goods funding, and open-source cryptographic libraries.
- Guided community excursions, local street food walks, and evening fireside chats exploring decentralized philosophy and decentralized physical infrastructure.

## Who should attend

The pop-up welcomes international developers, open-source researchers, crypto anthropologists, community builders, and Devcon attendees seeking community co-living and collaborative workspaces in Mumbai.

The residency runs daily from November 1 to November 6 in Mumbai, located within convenient commuting distance of the main Devcon venue at Bandra Kurla Complex.

Registration is open via ShanHaiWoo's Global Builder Village program. Space is allocated on an application-review basis to maintain an intimate, collaborative working environment.

name: Alchemy Meetings at Devcon Mumbai
description:
Alchemy hosts dedicated partner and developer meetings during Devcon week in Mumbai from Tuesday, November 3, through Friday, November 6, 2026. The sessions offer one-on-one technical architecture consultations with Alchemy's core engineering and product leadership.

## What to expect

These private meetings provide direct access to Alchemy specialists:
- Architecture review and node infrastructure optimization for high-throughput decentralized applications and decentralized finance protocols.
- Technical guidance on implementing Smart Account modular infrastructure, account abstraction (ERC-4337), and session keys.
- Strategic consultations regarding custom Rollup infrastructure, Subgraphs, webhooks, and developer tooling integrations.
- Direct feedback channels with Alchemy product managers to influence roadmap priorities and enterprise support tiers.

## Who should attend

Meetings are open to CTOs, engineering leads, protocol architects, and senior developers currently building or scaling Web3 projects who need tailored infrastructure advisory.

## Venue and schedule

Meetings take place across multiple hospitality suites near the Jio World Convention Centre in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), Mumbai, from November 3 to 6.

## Registration and admission

Builders must submit a meeting request form specifying their project details, technical stack, and specific discussion topics. Alchemy's team coordinates confirmed calendar slots and private suite access.

name: Field Station Rajasthan 2026
description:
Logos and Zu-Grama run Field Station at Dhun, a 500-acre regenerative site in Rajasthan, from October 23 to 31, 2026. The residency brings scientists, engineers, cryptographers, developers and community organizers together to build prototypes. The organizer's page specifies the October dates; the Devcon 8 calendar supplies the 2026 year. No daily start or finish time has been confirmed.

The program selects 30 residents. Scholarships cover eight nights of accommodation, food and drinks, on-site activities and the closing summit on October 30. Applicants can request domestic travel assistance. Rooms are shared, with five to seven people in single-sex rooms. The published application window was September 11 to 26.

Participants choose among the Logos Civic Prize, Logos Sovereignty and Privacy, Zu-Grama d/acc, and a non-builder track for activists, community organizers and artists. Technical work includes privacy-preserving blockchain, decentralized governance, censorship-resistant storage and secure payments. Creatives, designers and testers can also apply.

The schedule includes stand-ups, mentoring, dedicated build time, workshops and demos. Residents present prototypes at the closing summit. The strongest Logos-track prototypes are eligible for milestone-based grant funding. Applicants are asked to install Logos Basecamp, add its blockchain module and note the block height; an existing demo or prototype is helpful but not required.

name: Dev3pack Devcon Career Fair 2026
description:
Dev3pack's Career Fair takes place at Jio World Centre in Mumbai on November 6, 2026, inside the Devcon India campus. It is open to women and students with a valid Devcon ticket. The primary page confirms the day and venue but does not publish clock times.

The program includes a hiring floor with partner booths, career workshops on portfolios and interviews, a professional headshot setup with grooming, and a talent competition where builders can pitch and demo their work. A CV is optional but recommended for the application.

Career Fair registration is free, but a Devcon ticket is required to enter. Accepted applicants who do not already have a ticket can receive a $99 Day Pass voucher for Career Fair attendance or a 10% discount on a full four-day Devcon ticket. Application approval is required before those offers are sent.

Hiring partners must have at least three open roles and keep a team member at their booth throughout the day. Booths are free, places are limited, and participating companies receive a curated set of candidate profiles before the event. The organizer specifically welcomes applications from Indian startups.

name: Edge City India 2026
description:
Edge City India is a three-week popup village in Mandrem, North Goa, from October 11 to November 1, 2026. Founders, researchers, engineers and creators live and work around The Circle's beach-facing coworking hub. The program includes coworking, talks, workshops, salons and demo days.

The first week, October 11 to 17, focuses on new urbanism, energy, food systems and education. October 18 to 24 covers longevity and consciousness. The final week, October 25 to November 1, focuses on deep tech, AI, decentralized technologies, governance, policy and hackathons.

The announced Web3-related programs include Cross Margin Labs' Aqua0 DeFi residency, Hacker House Goa with 2:47PM Studio on October 28 to 31, and an October 30 Project Odin workshop with the Ethereum Foundation Funding Coordination team on sustainable funding for open-source software and digital infrastructure. Light DAO and SingularityNET also host a residency. These programs sit within the wider village rather than replacing its full date range.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Accepted applicants receive a ticket-purchase link, and payment confirms their place. Tickets include village programming, coworking and community activities, but not accommodation or most meals. Joining a residency is optional. Tickets are non-refundable; the organizer allows date changes or transfers to another attendee. Daily clock times are not confirmed for the village as a whole.
